style: set the scene in one or two plain sentences

candidates.angle: The self is friend or enemy depending on victory over the lower self
candidates.evidence: आत्मैवात्मना जितः (by whom the self has been conquered by the self)

candidates.angle: The true self is a friend only to the one who has conquered the lower self
candidates.evidence: येनात्मैवात्मना जितः (by whom the self has indeed been conquered by the self)

candidates.angle: The unconquered self behaves like an enemy to itself
candidates.evidence: अनात्मनस्तु शत्रुत्वे वर्तेतात्मैव शत्रुवत् (but for one not mastered, the self indeed acts like an enemy)

angle_en: The self is friend or enemy

en.intro: Krishna asks how one can be a friend to oneself. Listen to how he defines the inner battle.
en.notice: The word atma is used twice in one breath. The true self is a friend only when the lower self, the restless mind, is conquered by the true self. Without that victory, the self itself becomes the enemy.
en.next: Krishna says that for the one who has conquered the self, the supreme reality is present in heat and cold, pleasure and pain.
en.meaning: For one who has conquered the lower self by the true self, the true self is a friend. For one who has not conquered the lower self, the true self behaves like an enemy.

hi.intro: कृष्ण पूछते हैं कि मनुष्य अपना मित्र कैसे बन सकता है। सुनिए, वे आंतरिक युद्ध को कैसे परिभाषित करते हैं।
hi.meaning: जिसने अपने आप से अपने आप को जीत लिया है, उसके लिए आप ही अपना बन्धु है और जिसने अपने आप को नहीं जीता है, ऐसे अनात्माका आत्मा ही शत्रुतामें शत्रुकी तरह बर्ताव करता है।
hi.notice: यहाँ आत्मा शब्द का दो बार इस्तेमाल हुआ है। जब मनुष्य अपने निचले मन और इंद्रियों पर जीत हासिल कर लेता है, तभी उसका सच्चा स्वरूप मित्र बनता है। बिना इस जीत के, वही आत्मा शत्रु बन जाता है।
hi.next: कृष्ण कहते हैं कि जिसने अपने आप पर विजय पा ली है, उसके लिए परम सत्य हर सुख-दुख और मान-अपमान में हमेशा मौजूद रहता है।

issues: wrong_fact: "The battlefield is quiet for a moment, and the real fight is revealed." (This is unsupported. The Bhagavad Gita is set on the battlefield of Kurukshetra, but the text of verse 6 itself does not describe the battlefield as 'quiet for a moment' or the 'real fight' being 'revealed'. This is an invented narrative detail.)

borrowed: "Krishna now says that once the self is conquered, the supreme reality is present in every heat and cold, pleasure and pain." (This is borrowed from the NEXT verse (6.7). The 'next' field in the script presents the content of the following verse as if it were part of this verse's description.)
